clue.text: English crowd inside like this coffee

indicators.note: inside tells us the word for crowd sits within the word for like this

parts.note: so can mean 'in this way', like this
to press is to crowd or throng; a press is also a crowd

explanation.surface: Someone in a crowded café points at a cup: an English throng enjoying this kind of coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is a strong Italian-style coffee brewed by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Knife fight about it upset learner driver

indicators.note: about here means the fight word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight or scrap

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word it is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner driver, upset, gets into a fight over a knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' works as a reversal in a down clue, giving TI; 'about' then wraps the fight around TIL. 'Knife' looks like part of the brawl but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: Imaginary creature — draw one missing tail

parts.note: to draw a load is to drag or haul it

indicators.note: missing tail tells us the word for one loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A child tries to draw a mythical beast and leaves one without its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a fire-breathing monster of legend, a creature of myth rather than reality.

clue.text: Stand below with sly type

indicators.note: in a down clue, below places the stand word underneath the with letter

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painter's canvas

explanation.surface: An instruction to stand beneath someone sly, as if in a police line-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a weasel labels them a sneaky, untrustworthy person, after the animal's reputation.

clue.text: Pessimistic county defeated

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
beat means defeated, as in 'we beat them'

explanation.surface: A county's sports team has been defeated and is gloomy about it.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Downbeat describes a gloomy, negative mood, so it works as another word for pessimistic.

clue.text: Hostile about Diane, Oscar shows extreme foolishness

indicators.note: about means the hostile word wraps around the name and letter

parts.note: an icy reception is a coldly hostile one
Di is the short form of the name Diane
Oscar stands for O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone hostile to Diane, and Oscar too, displays great stupidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiocy is utter stupidity, the behaviour of an idiot, so it matches extreme foolishness.

clue.text: Fling with hard short unscrupulous type

parts.note: to shy is to fling or throw, as at a coconut shy

indicators.note: short tells us the hard word loses its final letter

parts.note: stern means hard or severe

explanation.surface: A fling with a harsh, curt person who turns out to be a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: A coconut shy is a British fairground stall where you throw balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a dishonest operator, typically a crooked lawyer, so an unscrupulous person.

clue.text: Old boy imprisoned by silly boy, lout

indicators.note: imprisoned by puts the old boy letters inside the jumbled word
silly suggests the word boy is jumbled into a daft order

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An old boy locked up by a silly youth, both of them louts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' is the anagram signal giving YBO, and 'imprisoned by' wraps that around the old boy.
explanation.definitionFit: A yobbo is British slang for a rowdy, aggressive young man, a hooligan.

clue.text: What mountaineer may seek to maintain crossing face of Everest

indicators.note: crossing means the two words span across the letter placed between them

parts.note: to hold an opinion is to maintain or assert it

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, so its first letter

explanation.surface: A climber on Everest's face looks for something to keep hold of.
explanation.definitionFit: A toehold is a small ledge or crack just big enough to support a climber's toe.

clue.text: Set off in time, ahead of scaffolder

indicators.note: ahead of in a down clue places the time letter above the scaffolder word

parts.note: a rigger erects scaffolding or rigging

explanation.surface: A building worker sets off on schedule, before the scaffolder arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off, cause it to start, as a trigger fires a gun.

clue.text: Part of a film about British anti-establishment figure

indicators.note: about means the film part goes around the letter

parts.note: a reel is one spool of film, part of a whole movie

explanation.surface: A section of a movie concerning a British dissident.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel resists authority and convention, so someone opposed to the establishment.

clue.text: Idols sang high for musical effect

indicators.note: high suggests the words are intoxicated and staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: Pop idols sing at a high pitch to produce a musical flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like pitch, but it is the anagram signal on IDOLS SANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a rapid slide through a series of notes, a recognised effect in music.

clue.text: Filming golf spectators in range

parts.note: shooting a film means filming it
the gallery is the crowd following players around a golf course

explanation.surface: A film crew shoots footage of golf fans within range of the cameras.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooting gallery is a place for target practice, the same sense as a firing range.

clue.text: Away representing Millwall, initially not playing well

parts.note: off means away, as in 'off on holiday'
for means representing, as in standing for a constituency

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A footballer playing away for Millwall, at first struggling with his game.
explanation.walkthrough: Millwall is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Off form is an idiom for performing below one's usual standard, especially in sport.

clue.text: Wave when tea's ready across lake?

indicators.note: across means the time phrase stretches over the lake letter, holding it inside

parts.note: four-ish, around four o'clock, is the traditional time for afternoon tea
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A host waves across the lake to signal that tea is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: British afternoon tea is traditionally taken at about four o'clock, hence 'four-ish'.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a sword or hat is to wave it about with a showy gesture.

clue.text: Search staff nurse, at first in cabin

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the cabin word

parts.note: a hut is a small cabin

indicators.note: at first means take the opening letter of nurse

explanation.surface: Staff search for a nurse who was first seen in a cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A manhunt is an organised search for a person, typically a fugitive.

clue.text: Prize wine shattered when shared out

parts.note: rosé is a light pink wine

indicators.note: out tells us the letters of shared are taken away from shattered

explanation.surface: A prize-winning bottle smashes, and its wine is handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes S,H,A and R,E,D (SHARED, in order) from SHATTERED, leaving TTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded as a prize at shows and competitions.

clue.text: Dessert wine and nuts are dished out on base

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the anagram above the base letter
dished out suggests the letters are served up in a new arrangement

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: Dessert wine and nuts are served after a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauterne is the sweet white wine of the Sauternes area of Bordeaux, drunk with dessert.

clue.text: Eastern celebrity catching our cracking train

indicators.note: catching means the outer pieces hold the jumbled word between them

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: cracking means the word our is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An Eastern celebrity is caught smashing up our train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' is the anagram signal giving URO; 'catching' sets it inside the outer pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurostar is the high-speed rail service through the Channel Tunnel linking London with Paris and Brussels.

clue.text: Unrestrained and violent action amazingly handled — no doubt by director, ultimately

indicators.note: amazingly suggests the words are thrown into wild disorder
ultimately means take the last letter of director

explanation.surface: A violent action scene was handled superbly, no doubt by the director.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood-and-thunder describes melodramatic violent excitement, as in sensational fiction or films.

clue.text: Important to keep can very cold

indicators.note: to keep means the important word holds the can word inside it

parts.note: big means important, as in a big decision
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: It matters to keep a can of drink chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting wind is sharply, painfully cold.

clue.text: Fellow leading ass

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
key means leading or principal, as in a key figure

explanation.surface: A man leads an ass along by its halter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ass is the animal also called a donkey; the two words name the same beast.

clue.text: Seeing union's leader boarding streetcar, a shock

indicators.note: boarding means getting onto the tram, so the letter goes inside it

parts.note: a streetcar is the American term for a tram

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Seeing a union leader climb aboard a streetcar comes as a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is a severe emotional shock or a deeply distressing experience.

clue.text: Daughter having extra port

parts.note: over means extra or left over, as in 'some over'

explanation.surface: A daughter has an extra glass of port.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is a port town in Kent, the main English harbour for Channel ferries.

clue.text: Natural at spinning, tropical spider

indicators.note: spinning suggests the letters whirl around into a new order

explanation.surface: A tropical spider is naturally good at spinning webs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' looks like web-making, but it is the anagram signal on NATURAL AT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantula is a large hairy spider found in warm regions of the world.

clue.text: The King altered lives

indicators.note: altered means the letters of lives are changed in order

explanation.surface: The King changed lives, a nod to the claim that he still lives.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley is widely known as the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: Beginning or ending of mountain climb

indicators.note: ending of means take the final letter of mountain

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A question about whether a mountain climb is starting or finishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning' is the definition, used as an adjective meaning just starting.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence, at an early, emerging stage.

clue.text: Source of wisdom, underground worker, Victor, with answer

parts.note: a miner works underground
Victor stands for V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A list of contributors to some fount of knowledge: a miner, Victor and an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom, so a mythological source of it.
